canvas.$description: Canvas — Page background, default surface — sets the off-white, paper-like base for the entire system

pure-white.$description: Pure White — Product UI panels, card surfaces, elevated content blocks — keeps content crisp against the off-white canvas

ink.$description: Ink — Primary headings and body text — softened black that reads warm rather than harsh

graphite.$description: Graphite — Secondary text, captions, nav labels, muted borders — the everyday gray for supporting copy

ash.$description: Ash — Tertiary text, disabled labels, faint dividers — the quietest gray in the system

outline.$description: Outline — Hairline borders, icon strokes, divider lines at thin weights — provides structural edges without tonal noise

shadow.$description: Shadow — Rare single-layer drop-shadow tone used for floating panels and the AI chat popover

signal-blue.$description: Signal Blue — Blue outline accent for tags, dividers, and focused UI edges. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

sky-tint.$description: Sky Tint — Notification pill background, subtle blue wash on interactive surfaces — the muted echo of Signal Blue used for non-action highlights

blush.$description: Blush — Decorative card surface — warm pink wash that frames product screenshots and feature blocks

lavender-mist.$description: Lavender Mist — Decorative card surface — soft purple wash for variety blocks and callout cards

mint-foam.$description: Mint Foam — Decorative card surface — cool teal wash for product mockup containers and accent cards

powder-blue.$description: Powder Blue — Decorative card surface — light blue wash used alongside the other pastels for tonal rhythm

butter.$description: Butter — Decorative card surface — warm yellow wash, the highest-contrast pastel used sparingly for emphasis cards

system-ui.$description: All UI and editorial copy — body at 16/400, subheadings at 18–20/500, section headings at 24–44/600, hero display at 56–64/600. The stack is system-ui (San Francisco / Segoe UI / Inter fallback) so the brand inherits the OS-native feel without licensing a webfont.
